title: Traffic-Aware Readiness Degradation & Localized Failover Playbook
creator: Maya Singh
description: Problem: Flapping readiness signals during short-lived traffic bursts cause the autoscaler to oscillate across regions, increasing tail latency and violating regional SLO windows. We also lack a consistent playbook for localized failover that minimizes cross-region traffic amplification and downstream capacity collapse. Goal: Implement a traffic-aware readiness degradation policy and a regional failover playbook that ties readiness/liveness behavior to request shape, token budgets, and circuit-breaker scoring so autoscaling remains stable and SLOs are preserved.
acceptance_criteria: New readiness policy is configurable per region and can be toggled via runtime feature flags
Autoscaler oscillation rate (scale up/down frequency) for synthetic burst tests is reduced by >= 60% compared to baseline
P99 tail latency during multi-region failover drill does not exceed SLO by more than 10%
Circuit breaker engages before cross-region reroutes cause capacity exhaustion and records events in Console dashboards
Runbook steps for localized failover are documented and validated in two on-call run drills
tasks: Design traffic-shape classifier for short vs sustained bursts and expose as a readiness heuristic
Add token-budget-aware readiness fence: track per-node token budget and mark degraded instead of NotReady when budget < threshold
Implement regional soft-failover flag that causes inbound traffic to route to local degraded pool before global reroute
Wire circuit-breaker scoring to readiness decisions so nodes with high evicted-request rates are proactively derated
Create synthetic canary workload harness that simulates burst amplification across regions
Add Console dashboard widgets: readiness-degradation-events, regional-derate-count, failover-latency timeline
Author runbook and coordinate two failover DR drills with SRE and product on-call
notes: Trade-offs: conservative degradation preserves availability but may temporarily reduce capacity; we prefer gradual derating windows to hard NotReady flips
We will prefer local derates over immediate cross-region reroute to avoid traffic amplification and egress costs
Failure modes: misclassified sustained load as burst — mitigated by minimum sustained-window of 30s and operator override
Metrics to track: readiness_state_transitions, node_token_budget_pct, regional_reroute_count, autoscale_frequency_per_min
